groups.cluster_summary: Ran 16 live searches across FMCSA, PHMSA, and USCG sources covering fine schedules, consultant pricing pages, dataset landing pages, and volume statistics. Surprises: FMCSA processed 71,000+ DataQs requests in 2024 (a real market for challenge drafting), HMSP oversight shifted from renewal-time thresholds to continuous SMS monitoring (which turns a biennial task into a monthly monitoring product), and USCG PSIX updates daily with 650,000+ vessels including foreign-flag PSC history. Receipts I could not obtain: published fee schedules for DataQs consultants, PHMSA special permit drafting, Sub M TPO audits, and pre-PSC attendance (all dollar figures for those are labeled estimates; the existence of the paid service category is receipted). The Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse candidate is returned as a kill: buyer spend is provable but per-driver data is consent-gated with no public entity-keyed lookup, failing g4 and g6.

atlas.segment: Mid-size for-hire carriers (50 to 1,000 trucks)
atlas.pain_point: Erroneous roadside violations inflate public CSA scores
atlas.description: Every roadside inspection feeds officer-entered violation data into SMS, where errors and non-attributable events score against the carrier for 24 months. Safety directors triage monthly SMS updates in spreadsheets, decide which violations to fight, and hand-write DataQs narratives with evidence uploads. Most fleets under-challenge because triage and drafting are slow and expertise-heavy.
atlas.boring_task: Reading monthly SMS violation extracts, matching them to inspection reports, and writing RDR narratives with evidence attachments in the DataQs portal
atlas.root_cause: FMCSA publishes raw officer-entered violation data with no agency-side QA, and the burden of proof for correction sits on the carrier within a 24 month scoring window
atlas.target_persona: Fleet safety director
atlas.current_workaround: Spreadsheet triage plus ad hoc consultant or attorney per challenge, or simply absorbing the score and the premium surcharge
atlas.frequency_note: SMS snapshot monthly; inspections weekly for fleets over 50 trucks; 71,000+ RDRs industry-wide in 2024
atlas.annual_impact_usd: 30,000 to 300,000 USD per mid-size carrier per year in premium delta plus consultant spend (premium ranges: Full Coverage LLC; retainer ranges: Moving Authority; blended figure labeled est.)
atlas.evidence_source_1: FMCSA, DataQs upgrade release citing 2024 request volume (2025), https://www.fmcsa.dot.gov/newsroom/fmcsa-upgrades-dataqs-program-improve-efficiency-and-transparency-safety-record
atlas.notes: Snapshot-diff labeling of removed violations is the defensible asset: it yields reversal-probability training data no consultant publishes. Competition is service firms (CNS, Trucksafe, CDL Consultants), not software; consultant fees are not published so per-challenge pricing is estimated.

atlas.boring_task: Recomputing rolling driver, vehicle, and hazmat OOS rates and crash rate from inspection records every month and reconciling them to the FMCSA methodology

groups.cluster_summary: Ran 17 live searches this session across ECHO/ICIS-NPDES DMR bulk files, California SMARTS public stormwater data, e-Manifest/RCRAInfo public manifest data, SDWIS/SDWA downloads, EPA's new per-PWSID Service Line Inventory report, and CalRecycle quarterly tonnage systems, plus fee benchmarks from environmental consultants, legal trade press, and construction lead platforms. Two surprises: EPA now publishes a national per-PWSID service line inventory report (a clean backbone for LSL products), and the March 2026 Paper Manifest Sunset Rule will make e-Manifest fully electronic, sharply increasing manifest data density for market intelligence. The strongest pattern in this cluster is that self-reported public compliance data (DMRs, SMARTS sampling, manifests, SDWIS violations) is already weaponized by plaintiffs and regulators while the regulated entities themselves lack an analytic view of their own exposure. Receipts I could not obtain: a hard annual count of CWA 60-day notice letters, published QISP fee schedules, and Waste Business Journal list prices; affected figures are labeled estimates. One candidate (RCRA inspection readiness) intentionally fails the repetition gate and is filed as kill-log material with a revival path as an add-on module to the e-Manifest product.

groups.cluster_summary: I ran 16 live searches across NYC DOB/OATH/LL97/LL11/LL87 compliance, NYC and Chicago open permit and violation datasets, and OSHA enforcement plus ITA injury data. Every backbone dataset URL was confirmed via search results this session (NYC Open Data Socrata slugs, Chicago Data Portal slugs, enforcedata.dol.gov, osha.gov ITA page), and penalty amounts came from nyc.gov, osha.gov, and named law or consulting firms. groups.cluster_summary: I ran 15 live searches across MA distribution (crosswalk, CPSC enrollment, agent compensation), SNF enforcement (PBJ penalties, CMP amounts, IDR process, deficiency datasets), home health (HHVBP, PDC refresh cadence, SHP benchmarking), and state licensing databases (Texas CCR childcare, California CDSS RCFE, Texas Rising Star). Biggest surprises: forced MA disenrollment hits 1 in 10 enrollees in 2026 (Johns Hopkins), 801 SNFs were one-starred on staffing in a single month for PBJ failures, and Texas gives childcare providers free state-funded Rising Star mentors, which killed the subsidy-defense candidate on buyer spend. Receipts I could not obtain: per-seat pricing for agency quoting platforms (SunFire is FMO-funded and free to agents), a KinderCare-specific licensing-compliance job description (used a Texas license-defense law firm as the spend receipt instead), and the exact Texas Rising Star screening frequency (guidelines PDF confirmed screening exists but cadence wording was not in snippets). Five of eight candidates key on CCN or CMS plan IDs, so NSigma's existing CCN and CMS pipeline infrastructure carries directly into three of them.

groups.cluster_summary: Ran 15 live searches across FDA, CMS, and NLM data surfaces this session. Strongest receipts: the FDA Data Dashboard refreshes compliance and inspection data every Monday with downloadable files, Vizient puts hospital drug-shortage labor at nearly 900M USD per year (2025 survey), FDA civil money penalty exposure for ClinicalTrials.gov noncompliance is 10,000 USD plus up to 10,000 USD per day (inflation adjusted), and early-2025 Import Alert 66-40 actions against Chinese API makers show supplier cutoffs are live, dateable events. Surprises: 67 to 70 percent of 510(k)s draw a first-cycle deficiency letter, and CLIA proficiency testing tightened to three events per year starting with the 2025 cycle, both of which sharpen repetition arguments. Receipts I could not obtain: hard day rates for mock FDA inspection consultants (only a 40,000 USD-plus project budget signal) and Cortellis/Newport list pricing, so those dollar figures are labeled estimates. Direct .gov fetches were avoided per sandbox rules, so cadence claims rest on search snippets of official pages.

Receipts I could not obtain: published per-supplier FSVP consultant price lists (firms quote custom), Steritech or EcoSure per-location audit pricing, a confirmed bulk CSV export for California cannabis licenses (search UI updates every 24 hours but bulk access appears scrape-based), and direct evidence of third-party spend on pesticide applicator credential tracking (that candidate leans on state fine schedules and in-house staffing, so I held its confidence at Medium). Cannabis fine figures come from a tier-3 advisory blog and are labeled as such. All dollar figures either carry the cited source or are explicitly labeled estimates.

groups.cluster_summary: Ran 13 targeted searches across NYC DOB/FDNY/DEP compliance regimes, California CSLB licensing data, OSHA ITA injury data, and EPA Section 608 refrigerant enforcement. Strongest pattern: NYC equipment compliance (gas piping LL152, elevator CAT1, boiler annual filings, FDNY violations, backflow devices) pairs per-device civil penalties with BBL/BIN-keyed open datasets, and NSigma already runs BBL-keyed NYC CRE infrastructure. Surprises: the famous LL152 $10,000 penalty was cut to $5,000 in 2021 ($1,500 for 3-family in 2024), and a DEP BACKFLOW PREVENTER open dataset exists but I could not verify its field contents this session. Receipts I could not obtain: a consolidated open-data dataset of LL152 GPS2 filings (only the DOB compliance-list spreadsheet plus DOB NOW portal status), update frequency for the boiler and backflow datasets, and any public per-appliance refrigerant leak data, which killed the Section 608 candidate on g4.

groups.cluster_summary: Ran 18 live searches across MSHA enforcement and open data, PHMSA enforcement dockets, FERC EQR and market-based-rate revocations, NERC notices of penalty, FCC broadband data collection, ULS licensing, and the Robocall Mitigation Database. Biggest surprises: the FCC's 2024-2025 RMD enforcement wave (1,200+ providers removed, all US carriers ordered to block 185 companies) created a brand-new carrier KYC compliance market whose backbone is a free public CSV; FERC publishes the names of EQR-delinquent sellers in Federal Register revocation orders, which is a ready-made lead list; and PHMSA publishes full enforcement case files including operator post-hearing briefs, proving operators pay outside counsel. Receipts I could not obtain: published price points for consultant fees (MSHA mock audits, BDC filing prep, EQR filing services), so those dollar figures are labeled estimates; current-fiscal-year MSHA penalty totals are also not directly receipted (best public figure is roughly 200M USD assessed in 2010 via trade press). All 8 candidates passed all six gates, though BDC cadence (semiannual filings plus rolling challenges) and NERC PDF parseability are the two softest passes.

groups.cluster_summary: Ran 20 live searches across export controls and trade, aviation and drones, and federal procurement. The biggest surprise: the February 20, 2026 Supreme Court decision striking down IEEPA tariffs and CBP's May 2026 CAPE refund portal (roughly 165B USD ordered refunded across about 330,000 importers and 53 million entries per law firm alerts), which turns tariff refund preparation into a deadline-driven, CSV-native wedge that fits a 6-week build. Confirmed official backbone URLs for the FAA releasable registry (daily CSV), FAA DRS, FAA Part 107 waivers-issued list, trade.gov CSL (daily 5 AM updates), FMC OTI list, USAspending award archive, and the GAO bid protest docket search. Receipts I could not obtain: published consultant DER hourly rates and CAMP maintenance-tracking subscription pricing (those figures are labeled estimates), the FAA waiver list update cadence, and per-organization repetition for Part 107 waiver filings, which killed the drone candidate on g3. Aviation-cluster pain evidence leans on trade press and vendor guides (tier 3), while trade and procurement candidates carry tier 1-2 receipts (CRS, GAO, OFAC enforcement reporting).

groups.cluster_summary: Ran 19 targeted searches across P&C insurance filings and market conduct, Davis-Bacon certified payroll, Clery and IPEDS compliance, property tax appeal, and veterinary DEA compliance. Surprises: SERFF Filing Access is fully public and free but trapped in 50 separate state portals with PDF attachments (ideal moat), Cook County publishes model-ready Socrata assessment data with monthly refreshes and rolling township appeal windows that make appeal prep a year-round monthly workflow, and the DEA bulk registrant file moved from a paid NTIS subscription to an annual application direct to DEA in 2020. Receipts I could not obtain: consultant price sheets (Perr&Knight, D. Stafford, LCPtracker all quote-only, so per-engagement dollar figures are labeled estimates), and no confirmed instance of an IPEDS fine actually being levied, which killed that candidate on g1 alongside its annual component cadence. The $14.1M FY2024 Davis-Bacon back-wage figure comes from an industry compliance guide citing DOL, tier 3 attribution.

g6_mvp_6wk.evidence: Public-data variance screen is buildable in 6 weeks, but the valuable half requires SIS integration, which drags the true MVP past the window for paying value.

atlas.segment: Small IR offices at mid-size institutions
atlas.pain_point: Seasonal IPEDS submission grind
atlas.description: One or two IR staff assemble a dozen federal survey components from student information system extracts three times a year, chasing edit failures and definition changes. The work is miserable but seasonal, and the penalty regime is theoretical: referrals to FSA rather than routine fines.
atlas.boring_task: Rebuilding enrollment and completions extracts to match IPEDS definitions and clearing NCES edit-check failures each collection window
atlas.root_cause: SIS data models do not match IPEDS reporting definitions, and mapping is redone by hand each cycle
atlas.target_persona: Director of Institutional Research (keyholder)
atlas.current_workaround: Spreadsheets, prior-year workbooks, occasional vendor modules (Precision Campus), AIR listserv folklore
atlas.frequency_note: Three collection windows per year; each of 12 components annual; fails weekly/monthly/quarterly test
atlas.annual_impact_usd: Staff burden of several hundred hours per institution per year (est.); fine authority up to 71,545 USD per violation (34 CFR 668.92) but no confirmed levies found
atlas.evidence_source_1: NCES, Statutory Requirements for Reporting IPEDS Data (2025), https://surveys.nces.ed.gov/ipeds/public/statutory-requirement
atlas.notes: Kill logged for the atlas: real burden, public data, identifiable key (UnitID), but no acute penalty in practice and annual cadence. Revisit if the 2025 executive-order push toward remedial action for late/inaccurate submissions turns into actual enforcement.

candidates.name: Commercial Property Tax Appeal Evidence Packet Generator
candidates.vertical: Commercial appraisal, assessment, and property tax representation
candidates.wedge_artifact: Per-parcel appeal evidence packet: assessment-equity comp grid (lack-of-uniformity analysis against matched parcels), sales comps, assessment-ratio statistics, prefilled appeal narrative for the Assessor/Board of Review form, and a deadline calendar for every parcel in the portfolio. Owner income data (rent rolls) is an optional upsell for income-approach arguments, not required for the MVP.
candidates.lead_magnet: Free PIN or BBL lookup: over-assessment screen score with estimated annual savings and the parcel's next filing window.
candidates.entity_key: County parcel ID: Cook County PIN, NYC BBL (Harris County account number as expansion)

backbone_source.name: Cook County Assessor open data (Assessed Values, Parcel Universe, Parcel Sales, Appeals)
backbone_source.claimed_format: CSV / Socrata API
backbone_source.claimed_update_freq: Monthly refresh; values change through Board of Review certification

supporting_sources.name: Cook County assessment and appeal calendar
supporting_sources.note: Rolling township windows that drive the product's deadline engine

supporting_sources.note: Second launch market; direct NSigma BBL infrastructure overlap

supporting_sources.name: Cook County Assessor GitHub (ccao-data)

buyer.title: Principal at property tax consulting/law firm; secondarily asset managers
buyer.org_type: Property tax consultants, certiorari attorneys, CRE owners

candidates.pain_mechanism: Tax rep firms win by filing well-evidenced appeals inside rolling township and county windows; every packet (equity comps, sales comps, ratio math, narrative) is hand-built by analysts per parcel, which caps how many contingency-fee engagements a firm can take per window and leaves savings on the table for owners who never appeal.
candidates.status_quo_cost: Consultants charge 25-50% of first-year tax savings as contingency (NTPTS and peers); analyst time per commercial packet runs hours to days; one NYC certiorari firm reports over 1B USD in cumulative refunds obtained, indicating the fee pool at stake.
candidates.nsigma_overlap: STRONG: NSigma already operates BBL-keyed NYC CRE data infrastructure; NYC certiorari (Jan 15 to Mar 1 window, Tax Class 4) is a natural second market on existing rails.

g1_acute_pain.evidence: Over-assessment is direct cash loss: NYC Tax Class 4 commercial appeals with professional evidence achieve 20-50% reductions, and one certiorari firm reports over 1B USD in refunds obtained for clients; missing a window forfeits a full year of savings.

g3_repetition.evidence: Cook County opens appeal windows on a rolling schedule, 4 to 5 townships per month with roughly 30-day windows, followed by separate Board of Review windows; a tax rep firm therefore preps packets every month year-round, and multi-county firms stack NYC (Jan-Mar) and Texas (May) seasons on top.

g6_mvp_6wk.evidence: Cook County data is already clean and API-served (the Assessor even publishes its models on GitHub); comp-grid generation, ratio stats, and PDF packet output for one county is comfortably a 6-week build reusing NSigma's parcel-data patterns.

atlas.segment: Property tax consulting and certiorari firms; CRE owners with multi-parcel portfolios
atlas.pain_point: Hand-built appeal evidence packets cap appeal volume
atlas.description: Analysts at tax rep firms manually pull assessor records, select equity and sales comps, compute ratio statistics, and write appeal narratives parcel by parcel against rolling monthly township deadlines. Packet quality drives reduction size and contingency revenue, so throughput is the binding constraint on firm growth, and unrepresented owners simply overpay.
atlas.boring_task: Pulling comparable parcel records and assembling comp grids, ratio calculations, and narrative boilerplate for each appeal filing
atlas.root_cause: Assessment, sales, and appeal data are public but per-parcel workflows are manual because no tool joins roll data, comps, ratio math, and jurisdiction-specific filing formats
atlas.target_persona: Principal or senior analyst at a property tax consulting or certiorari firm
atlas.current_workaround: Analyst spreadsheets, county portal lookups, some firms build internal scripts; owners without reps do nothing and overpay
atlas.frequency_note: Monthly: Cook County opens 4-5 townships per month with ~30-day windows plus Board of Review rounds; NYC window Jan 15 to Mar 1; Texas May 15; firms cycle jurisdictions year-round
atlas.annual_impact_usd: Consultant contingency fees of 25-50% of savings (NTPTS); single NYC firm reports 1B+ USD cumulative refunds (Goldburd McCone, firm claim); per-parcel commercial savings commonly 5,000 to 500,000 USD per year (est.)
atlas.evidence_source_1: Cook County Assessor's Office, Assessment and Appeal Calendar (2026), https://www.cookcountyassessoril.gov/assessment-calendar-and-deadlines
atlas.notes: Direct NSigma overlap via BBL-keyed NYC infrastructure. Competitive field exists at residential (Ownwell, TaxRival) which validates the wedge; commercial equity-grid packets for rep firms remain analyst-built. Sell to firms as throughput software, not to owners against the firms.

candidates.name: Veterinary Group DEA and License Compliance Tracker with Audit-Prep Packet
candidates.vertical: Veterinary multi-site practice compliance (controlled substances and licensure)
candidates.hybrid_note: Public layer: state vet board license status and discipline plus DEA registration validity per vet and per premise delivers a day-1 roster audit (expirations, premise/registrant mismatches, missing state controlled substance registrations) from a pasted clinic list. Private layer: PIMS dispensing and inventory logs (Cornerstone, ezyVet exports, moderate to painful) add weekly log reconciliation and biennial inventory prep, which is the sticky part.
candidates.wedge_artifact: Monthly multi-site compliance packet: licenses and DEA registrations expiring in 30/60/90 days by clinic, state CS registration gaps, disciplinary-action alerts, mock DEA audit checklist tuned to current enforcement themes, and a biennial inventory scheduler; log-reconciliation exception report once PIMS data is connected.
candidates.lead_magnet: Free group roster audit: upload clinic and DVM list (or DEA numbers), get expirations, lapses, and premise/registration mismatches in one PDF.
candidates.entity_key: State veterinary license number plus DEA registration number (per veterinarian and per registered premise)

buyer.title: Director of Compliance / Director of Pharmacy
buyer.org_type: Veterinary consolidator or regional group (10-500 clinics)

candidates.pain_mechanism: Every clinic is a DEA registrant handling ketamine, opioids, and euthanasia solution; recordkeeping gaps are the most-cited violation at up to 15,691 USD per violation with an average of 11 violations per inspected practice (industry estimate), and a lapsed license or DEA registration makes every dispense at that site unlawful. Consolidators track hundreds of DVM licenses and premise registrations across 50 state rule sets in spreadsheets.
candidates.status_quo_cost: DOJ/DEA settlements with individual vet practices ran 15,000 USD (Dedham, 2022), 90,000 USD (Marietta GA), and 226,000 USD plus registration surrender (Colorado); groups pay ex-DEA consultants (Titan Group) for mock audits and buy log software (VetSnap, Cubex) per site.
candidates.nsigma_overlap: No shared dataset, but the multi-site, entity-keyed license/compliance tracking pattern is identical to NSigma's CMS CCN senior living work.

g1_acute_pain.evidence: DEA settlements with veterinary practices are documented and specific: 15,000 USD (Dedham MA, 2022, recordkeeping), 90,000 USD (Marietta GA), 226,000 USD plus DEA registration surrender (Colorado); recordkeeping violations run up to 15,691 USD each.

atlas.segment: Multi-site veterinary groups and consolidators
atlas.pain_point: Lapsed registrations and log gaps across dozens of clinics
atlas.description: Compliance leads at vet groups track hundreds of DVM licenses, premise DEA registrations, and state controlled substance registrations in spreadsheets while each clinic hand-logs ketamine and opioid usage. A single missed renewal or sloppy logbook surfaces in a DEA inspection as stacked per-violation penalties and, in bad cases, registration surrender that halts surgical services at that site.
atlas.boring_task: Checking each vet and premise against state board portals and DEA validation one at a time and chasing clinics for renewal proof each month
atlas.root_cause: Licensure and registration truth lives in 50 unconnected state portals plus a DEA database with no group-level monitoring layer, while dispensing logs sit on paper or in per-site PIMS
atlas.target_persona: Director of Compliance at a 10-500 clinic veterinary group
atlas.current_workaround: Spreadsheets, per-site log binders, Titan Group mock audits, VetSnap/Cubex at some sites
atlas.frequency_note: Daily-to-weekly log reconciliation; monthly renewal cycles across any group of 10+ clinics; biennial DEA inventory per registrant
atlas.annual_impact_usd: Documented per-practice settlements 15,000 to 226,000 USD (DEA/DOJ 2022-2024); up to 15,691 USD per recordkeeping violation with an industry-estimated 11 violations per practice (Titan Group)
atlas.evidence_source_1: U.S. DEA, press release on Dedham veterinarian 15,000 USD recordkeeping settlement (2022), https://www.dea.gov/press-releases/2022/09/21/dedham-veterinarian-agrees-pay-15000-settlement-resolve-allegations
atlas.notes: Bulk DEA registrant data requires an annual application to DEA (post-NTIS), so plan on per-number public validation for MVP and apply for the CSA database in parallel; consolidation wave (NVA, Mission, Thrive) concentrates budget in a small number of nameable buyers.
